I've made the change, but I could not build or run the app here, so it is unverified on a device.

**The cause:** The debug build talks to the local dev API at `https://10.0.2.2:8443/`, which uses a certificate signed by the self-signed dev CA in `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`. Android only trusts publicly known CAs by default, so the handshake failed with "Trust anchor for certification path not found."

**The fix (debug build only, release unchanged):**
- `app/src/debug/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem`: a copy of the dev CA. Android can't reference files outside `res/`, so it has to live here.
- `app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`: trusts the system CAs plus `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca`.
- `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`: a manifest overlay that sets `android:networkSecurityConfig` on the application. Because it's in the `debug` source set, the release build never sees it.

**Things to check:**
- I copied the PEM by hand. Please confirm `app/src/debug/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem` matches `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem` byte for byte. If the cert ever changes, both copies need updating. A mismatch would show up as the same trust-anchor error.
- The CA is valid until 2036, so the copy shouldn't expire soon.
- No code changes were needed in `CatalogClient.kt`.
